slides: Open the chapter by refusing to treat signal processing and optimization as a bag of unrelated techniques. PCA, ICA, NMF, sparse paths, barriers, and scoring rules all choose a representation, constraint, metric, or score that makes hidden structure inspectable.

The route slide gives students a checklist. Each application changes the geometry in a different way: covariance axes, non-Gaussian rotations, positive cones, L one diamonds, barrier metrics, or proper scoring games. The unifying habit is to ask which invariant certifies the picture.

PCA and whitening start from covariance geometry. Eigenvectors draw the ellipse axes, whitening removes second-order scale, and online learning becomes a path on the unit circle. The checks verify whitening to identity covariance and show the learned axis reaches within about a degree.

ICA begins after whitening has removed covariance preferences. At that point rotations remain ambiguous unless non-Gaussianity supplies a contrast. The figure and checks show that non-Gaussian sources recover a meaningful demixing direction, while a Gaussian replacement flattens the contrast.

NMF changes the problem from orthogonal axes to positive cones. Multiplicative updates preserve nonnegativity when initialized inside the cone, and the residual drop confirms that the factorization improves. This is a constraint geometry, not merely another matrix decomposition.

Sparse regression is the cleanest constraint picture. The L one ball is a diamond, so the constrained solution path follows polygonal geometry under the quadratic metric. The radial shortcut looks tempting but is provably suboptimal in the checked anisotropic metric example.

Barrier methods introduce geometry through the Hessian of the barrier and dual coordinates through its gradient. The square barrier example keeps slacks positive, bends the primal central path toward the boundary, and becomes a straight ray in dual coordinates up to numerical residual.

The Hyvarinen score slide introduces a different kind of geometry: estimation as a game scored by derivatives of log density. The useful feature is normalization-constant invariance, and the numerical identity check confirms that the displayed divergence equals the expected squared score-field mismatch.

Use the failure-mode slide as an active lab prompt. Each artifact has a way to break: Gaussian ICA flattens contrast, NMF can leave the cone if initialized badly, radial sparse shrinkage can look plausible but lose objective value, and barrier paths fail when slacks vanish.

Close with the application-level synthesis. These methods are unified by geometry plus checks: covariance and whitening identities, demixing correlations, nonnegative factors, feasible sparse paths, positive barrier metrics, dual ray identities, and proper score identities. The artifacts make each claim inspectable.
